text:
maya: taking handoff in ~10m :wave: current active incident is #523 — kv-cache evictions causing request slowdowns. aj you're primary now, kevin secondary. i'll be primary at 10:05. any blockers?
aj: quick status — root cause looks like a canary deploy that increased write pressure; cache eviction storm + cold misses. p95 at peak ~720ms (SLO is 300ms). we've rolled back the canary in canary-pool and started a controlled cache-size bump.

important: to avoid duplicate pages during the handoff i'm temporarily raising the p95 alert threshold to 800ms for 30m while we stabilize. i set a reminder to restore it. pm/customer messaging sent. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache

commands i ran:```
opsctl deploy rollback --service cache-proxy --to canary-2026-03-14
opsctl infra patch --name cache-pool --json '{"target_size": 2.5}'
opsctl alerts update --alert latency.slo.kv_cache --threshold 800 --duration 30m --reason "handoff suppress duplicate pages"
```

incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT triggered: latency.slo.kv_cache p95 breached at 1759123380 — paging oncall

maya: ack. thanks aj. can you paste the exact opsctl command you used to change the alert? i may need to revert sooner if rollback doesn't hold.
aj: pasted above — feel free to run the same with --threshold 300 to restore. also note we muted noisy downstream alert groups:```
opsctl alerts silence --group cache-backpressure --duration 30m --reason "handoff mute"
```

kevin: i'll be secondary. if rollback flaps i'll take infra tasks (increase node counts, watch eviction rates). assign me the follow-up runbook entries.
sam: (FYI) i've notified growth/pm and support. we sent a customer-impact update for top 10 affected tenants. please add a short blameless note in the incident doc after handoff.
oncall-bot: shift-handoff: maya primary 10:05-18:05, kevin secondary. detected potential coverage gap 12:00-13:00 (lunch) — please confirm coverage or request backup.
maya: i'll cover lunch. @kevin can you be backup if i step out?
kevin: confirmed, reachable via phone + slack.
aj: after revert metrics so far: p50 45ms, p95 250ms, errors 0.04%. holding for another 10m before removing mitigations.
maya: great. i'll take over now. aj — any open follow-ups? paste checklist and pending items so i can triage if something flaps.
aj: checklist: 1) monitor p95, 2) confirm no eviction spikes >10% for 15m, 3) validate downstream queue depth < 200. pending: update autoscaler to new limits if we see sustained pressure. i've left debug logs at https://redwood.internal/logs/incident-523 (team access).
maya: noted. i've scheduled a reminder to restore the SLO alert to 300ms in ~28m. setting local watch:```
# quick check loop
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do curl -sS https://metrics.redwood/internal/v1/p95?service=kv_cache; sleep 180; done
```

oncall-bot: reminder created: restore-alerts (will fire in 28m) — opsctl link: opsctl://alerts/latency.slo.kv_cache/restore

maya: handoff complete. summary for the log: took primary at 10:05, rollback applied, temporary alert threshold raised to 800ms for 30m to reduce noise, cache size increased, p95 recovered under SLO, customers notified. follow-ups: add autoscaler tuning PR, expand runbook section for canary rollback steps, postmortem doc assignment to aj + kevin. cc @sam. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident #523 status changed -> monitoring.
maya: leaving a short note in the incident doc then signing off from thread. if anything odd appears ping me or escalate to sam.
